He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton Bluejays]]. ==High school career== Zegarowski attended [[Hamilton-Wenham Regional High School|Hamilton-Wenham]], where as a freshman he averaged 20 points per game. Alongside twin brother Max, Marcus led the team to an undefeated season and the school's first-ever Division 4 state basketball championship. Both Zegarowskis transferred to [[Tilton School]] in New Hampshire for their sophomore season.{{cite news |last1=Nicastro |first1=Dom |title=Hamilton-Wenham Zegarowski brothers make the move to Tilton |url=https://www.patriotledger.com/article/20160107/SPORTS/160107316 |accessdate=March 20, 2020 |work=[[The Patriot Ledger]] |date=January 7, 2016}} Marcus averaged 23 points, five rebounds, and six assists per game as a junior and had a season-high 37 points against [[Proctor Academy]]. He led the team to the Class AA championship game before losing to [[Cushing Academy]], and he was named to the All-NEPSAC AA first team. As a senior, Zegarowski was named NEPSAC AA player of the year and scored a career-high 57 points in a 118–116 double overtime win over the [[South Kent School]].{{cite news |last1=Levinsky |first1=Greg |title=Hamilton's Marcus Zegarowski is on point for Creighton men's basketball |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/globelocal/2020/01/31/hamilton-marcus-zegarowski-point-for-creighton-men-basketball/BWXFT3qtAyhr8zdP48oFuO/story.html |accessdate=March 20, 2020 |work=[[Boston Globe]] |date=January 31, 2020}} He scored 24 points in a 99–92 win over [[St. Andrew's School (Rhode Island)|St. Andrew's School]] as Tilton won the Class AA championship.{{cite news |last1=Giannino |first1=Nick |title=REVVED-UP RAMS: Zegarowski brothers wrapping up Tilton careers in style |url=https://www.salemnews.com/sports/revved-up-rams-zegarowski-brothers-wrapping-up-tilton-careers-in/article_1036bc77-f1a2-59c7-81de-83168262fb88.html |accessdate=March 20, 2020 |work=[[The Salem News]] |date=March 8, 2018}} Zegarowski committed to playing college basketball for [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]] over offers from [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]], [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]], and [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]]. ==College career== On February 3, 2019, Zegarowski fractured his hand and missed three games.{{cite news |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Injury won't stop Creighton freshman Marcus Zegarowski from lending a hand |url=https://www.omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/injury-won-t-stop-creighton-freshman-marcus-zegarowski-from-lending/article_607179ff-4633-5984-acad-e4fdd33f9eb4.html |accessdate=March 20, 2020 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=February 19, 2019}} As a freshman, Zegarowski became Creighton's starting point guard and averaged 10.4 points, 3.4 assists, and 3.2 rebounds per game. He was named to the [[Big East Conference|Big East]] All-Freshman Team. Zegarowski had an offseason hip injury that forced him to miss the team's exhibition trip to Australia.{{cite news |last1=Giannino |first1=Nick |title=Zegarowski healthy and eager to step up for Creighton |url=https://www.salemnews.com/sports/zegarowski-healthy-and-eager-to-step-up-for-creighton/article_59c425d1-75a8-5931-943a-7f6e71fd5562.html |accessdate=March 20, 2020 |work=[[The Salem News]] |date=October 10, 2019}} Zegarowski scored a career-high 32 points and had five assists and two steals on November 30, in a 83–76 overtime win over [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]].{{cite news |title=Zegarowski, Creighton beat No. 12 Texas Tech 83–76 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401186914 |accessdate=March 20, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 30, 2019}} On February 23, 2020, he made all seven three-point attempts en route to 25 points in an 81–59 win over [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]].{{cite news |title=Zegarowski can't miss, No. 15 Creighton routs No. 21 Butler |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168311 |accessdate=March 20, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 23, 2020}} On March 7, Zegarowski suffered a right knee injury during the game against [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]], but still managed to post 23 points, six rebounds, and five assists in the win.{{cite news |title=Creighton's Marcus Zegarowski doubtful for Big East tourney with knee injury |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28873421/creighton-marcus-zegarowski-doubtful-big-east-tourney-knee-injury?device=featurephone |accessdate=March 20, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=March 8, 2020}} He underwent arthroscopic surgery after the game, ending his season. Zegarowski averaged 16.1 points and 5 rebounds per game as a sophomore, shooting 42.4 percent from three-point range.{{cite news |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Creighton's Marcus Zegarowski undergoes surgery; status for NCAA tournament unclear |url=https://www.omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/creighton-s-marcus-zegarowski-undergoes-surgery-status-for-ncaa-tournament/article_e01146fd-8366-5ece-8b14-281bee0f114a.html |accessdate=March 20, 2020 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=March 11, 2020}} He was named to the Second Team All-Big East{{cite news |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Creighton's Ty-Shon Alexander named to All-Big East first team; Marcus Zegarowski on second team |url=https://www.omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/creighton-s-ty-shon-alexander-named-to-all-big-east/article_bef7044f-6edc-5c13-b409-cf4114a0a81d.html |accessdate=March 20, 2020 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=March 8, 2020}} and Second Team All-American by [[NBC Sports]].{{cite news |last1=Dauster |first1=Rob |title=NBC Sports College Basketball All-American Teams |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/03/20/college-basketball-all-american-teams/ |accessdate=March 20, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=March 20, 2020}} Coming into his junior season, Zegarowski was named Preseason Big East Player of the Year.{{cite news |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Marcus Zegarowski named Big East preseason player of year; Jays picked second |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/marcus-zegarowski-named-big-east-preseason-player-of-year-jays-picked-second/article_042dd0c0-36c6-5550-87b4-8eee97515cbb.html |accessdate=October 31, 2020 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=October 28, 2020}} He averaged 15.8 points, 4.3 assists, 3.6 rebounds and 1.3 steals per game and led the Big East with 80 three-pointers. Zegarowski was named to the First Team All-Big East and led the Bluejays to the Sweet 16 of the NCAA Tournament before falling to [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]]. On April 13, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite news |title=Creighton star PG Marcus Zegarowski declares for NBA draft |url=https://nationalpost.com/pmn/sports-pmn/creighton-star-pg-marcus-zegarowski-declares-for-nba-draft |access-date=August 3, 2021 |work=[[National Post]] |agency=[[Reuters]] |date=April 13, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Long Island Nets (2021–2022)=== Zegarowski was selected in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] with the 49th pick by the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite news|first=Nick|last=Giannino|title=Zegarowski reflects on being drafted; eager to get started with Nets|url=https://www.salemnews.com/sports/zegarowski-reflects-on-being-drafted-eager-to-get-started-with-nets/article_25205acb-a675-5caf-9c64-e97315830cd5.html|work=[[The Salem News]]|date=August 3, 2021|access-date=August 3, 2021}} Zegarowski was later included in the roster of the [[Brooklyn Nets]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets announce summer League roster|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/08/03/brooklyn-nets-announce-summer-league-roster|website=NBA.com|date=August 3, 2021|access-date=August 6, 2021}} On October 25, 2021, Zegarowski was included in the training camp roster of the [[Long Island Nets]].{{cite web|title=Long Island Nets announce training camp roster|url=https://longisland.gleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-announce-training-camp-roster-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=October 25, 2021}} On March 18, 2022, the [[Long Island Nets]] waived Zegarowski.{{cite web|title=Long Island Nets acquire Alex Robinson|url=https://longisland.gleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-acquire-alex-robinson|website=NBA.com|date=March 18, 2022|access-date=March 18, 2022}} On September 25, 2022, the [[Brooklyn Nets]] signed Zegarowski to an Exhibit 10 deal.{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Milholen|title=Nets sign Marcus Zegarowski to wrap up training camp roster|url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/nba/nets-sign-marcus-zegarowski-to-wrap-up-training-camp-roster/ar-AA12eEvJ|website=MSN.com|date=September 25, 2022|access-date=November 2, 2022}} On November 4, 2022, Zegarowski was named to the opening night roster for the [[Long Island Nets]].{{cite web|title=Long Island Nets Complete 2022-23 Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/long-island-nets-complete-2022-23-roster/n-5895915|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 4, 2022|access-date=November 4, 2022}} ===Windy City Bulls (2022)=== On November 12, 2022, Zegarowski was traded to the [[Windy City Bulls]] in exchange for [[Vrenz Bleijenbergh]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 22, 2022}} ===Austin Spurs (2022–2023)=== On December 22, 2022, Zegarowski was traded from Windy City to the [[Austin Spurs]]. ===Vanoli Cremona (2023–2024)=== On September 19, 2023, Zegarowski signed with [[Guerino Vanoli Basket|Vanoli Cremona]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]].{{cite web|title=Marcus Zegarowski è un nuovo giocatore della Vanoli Cremona|url=https://www.vanolibasket.it/marcus-zegarowski-e-un-nuovo-giocatore-della-vanoli-cremona/|website=VanoliBasket.it|date=September 19, 2023|access-date=September 19, 2023|language=Italian}} ===Later years and retirement=== On March 19, 2024, Zegarowski signed with [[Ironi Ness Ziona B.C.|Ironi Ness Ziona]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{cite web |title=Marcus Zegarowski joins Ironi Ness Ziona |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/marcus-zegarowski-joins-ironi-ness-ziona/ |website=Sportando |access-date=March 19, 2024 |date=March 19, 2024}} On August 8, 2024, Zegarowski signed with [[BC Oostende|Filou Oostende]] of the [[BNXT League]].{{cite web|title=Welcome Marcus|url=https://bcoostende.be/nieuws/welcome-marcus/|website=BCOostende.be|date=August 8, 2024|access-date=August 19, 2024|language=nl}} On February 26, 2025, he signed with [[Legia Warsaw (basketball)|Legia Warsaw]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]] (PLK).{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/marcus-zegarowski-joins-legia-kosz/|title=Marcus Zegarowski joins Legia Kosz|last=|first=|date=February 26, 2025|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=February 28, 2025}} Due to injuries, Zegarowski never played a single minute for any of the three teams. On March 25, 2025, he announced his retirement on Instagram.{{Cite Instagram |user=marcuszeg_ |postid=DHoPiiJNZGb |title=I gave this game everything I had. Zegarowski has a twin brother, Max, who also plays Division I basketball for [[Stonehill Skyhawks men's basketball|Stonehill College.]] Both his parents, Zach and Amanda, played basketball in high school, and Amanda is a basketball coach.{{cite web |last1=Giannino |first1=Nick |title=Tilton Tough: Zegarowski brothers continue their basketball dominance in prep school |url=https://www.salemnews.com/sports/tilton-tough-zegarowski-brothers-continue-their-basketball-dominance-in-prep/article_4b430f3e-579e-5bd5-91a8-03898bb3e696.html |website=[[The Salem News]] |accessdate=March 11, 2020 |date=March 30, 2017}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://gocreighton.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/marcus-zegarowski/6380 Creighton Bluejays bio] {{2021 NBA draft}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Zegarowski, Marcus}} [[Category:1998 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Italy]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Austin Spurs players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Essex County, Massachusetts]] [[Category:BC Oostende players]] [[Category:Brooklyn Nets draft picks]] [[Category:Creighton Bluejays men's basketball players]] [[Category:Long Island Nets players]] [[Category:People from Hamilton, Massachusetts]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Vanoli Cremona players]] [[Category:Windy City Bulls players]]
